name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Shephatiah. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, highlighting his place within the Judean lineage. There are no additional notes or detailed narrative about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah means 'YHWH has said,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's authority. This name is recorded in Nehemiah 11:4 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Amariah as the son of Shephatiah and infers that Zechariah was his father, establishing a direct paternal line. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, as documented in Nehemiah 11:4. His mention contributes to the preservation of the post-exilic community's lineage, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people. Although not prominent in narrative events, his record affirms the faithful restoration of Israel's tribal heritage.
